title: Ask for Reviews Before the Year Ends
meta: Reviews decide who gets the call. Run a focused December push to ask this year's happy customers before you head into 2027. Here's exactly how.
short: A focused December review push, because reviews decide the call.
statLabel: the easiest month to stack reviews

body.answer: Run a December review push. Ask every happy customer from this year before it closes out, because reviews are what decide the call going into 2027.
body.html:
You did good work all year. Most of those customers would leave you a review if you asked — but you didn't, because you were busy. December is your window. Things slow down, the jobs are still fresh, and a pile of new reviews sets up your whole next year.

Why bother? Because most homeowners read online reviews before choosing a contractor, and most won't seriously consider a shop under 4 stars (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey). Reviews aren't vanity. They're the thing that decides whether a stranger calls you or the next guy.

body.h2: Make a list of this year's happy customers
body.answer: Pull the jobs that went well and the customers who were clearly happy. That's your review push list.
body.html:
Open your job list or invoicing and go back through the year. Flag the customers who were genuinely happy — the ones who said thanks, tipped, or referred someone. Those are the people who'll say yes.

Don't overthink it. Twenty happy customers is plenty to move your star count and your review total. You're not spamming everyone; you're asking the people who already like you.

body.answer: Text them a direct review link with a one-line ask. Short beats polished. Make it one tap to leave the review.
body.html:
Keep it short and human: 'Hey, this is Mike from the plumbing job back in October — thanks again. Would you mind leaving us a quick Google review? Takes 30 seconds, here's the link.' Then paste the direct link.

The direct link is the trick. Don't make them search for you. One tap to the review box. Our guide on how to get more Google reviews has the wording that works and how to get that link, and the reviews hub covers what to do with them once they land.

body.h2: Answer fast and keep it going
body.answer: Reply to every review, good or bad, and make asking a habit so you never go into a new year light on reviews again.
body.html:
When reviews come in, reply to them — all of them. A quick thanks on the good ones and a calm, professional reply on any tough ones shows the next homeowner you're a real, responsive shop. Speed shows up here too: fast, present businesses win, same as responding in 5 minutes instead of 30 makes you up to 100x more likely to connect with a lead (Lead Response Management study, Prof. James Oldroyd).

Then don't stop in January. Build asking for a review into the end of every job so next December you're not playing catch-up. Want a system that asks for you automatically? Talk to Aaron.

faq.q: Is it too pushy to ask for reviews in December?
faq.a: No. You're asking happy customers for 30 seconds of help. Keep it short and give them a direct link and most will say yes.

faq.q: How many reviews do I need?
faq.a: More than your competitor, and enough to hold above 4 stars. Most homeowners won't seriously consider a shop under 4 stars (BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey), so protect that number.
Yes, every one. A quick thanks on the good ones and a calm reply on the hard ones tells the next homeowner you're responsive and real.
